brief.headline: Memory complex enters bear territory as Samsung record profit fails to satisfy; HBM3E pricing holding but buyers balking at conventional DRAM/NAND surge
brief.summary: <cite index="41-7,41-8,41-9">Micron, Samsung, and SK Hynix all fell more than 20% from recent highs despite Samsung's operating profit estimate of $59 billion and sales of $113 billion.</cite> <cite index="38-10,42-12">Samsung fell 9% and SK Hynix dropped 14.6% intraday Tuesday, even as Samsung projected a 19-fold jump in Q2 operating profit.</cite> <cite index="42-15,42-17">Analysts still see support from tight memory supply through Q3, with JPMorgan expecting memory pricing to drive H2 earnings as demand exceeds supply despite growing customer resistance.</cite> <cite index="17-2">TrendForce projects conventional DRAM contract prices to rise 13-18% QoQ in Q3 2026, with NAND up 10-15%, a marked slowdown from Q2's ~60% jumps.</cite> <cite index="15-22">DDR4 spot rose 3.57% to $34.80 in early June, but suppliers' higher quotes made buyers hesitant to chase further increases.</cite>
brief.pair_trade_view: <cite index="2-12,2-18">SK Hynix holds 62% HBM shipment share as of Q2 2025, with Goldman and UBS forecasting SK to maintain 50%+ total HBM share through 2026 and secure ~70% HBM4 share for NVIDIA's Rubin platform.</cite> <cite index="1-19,1-20,1-21">SK leads at 50-55% overall HBM market share, followed by Samsung at 35-40%, with SK first to mass-produce HBM3E and securing the majority of NVIDIA supply contracts, while Samsung is ramping 12-high HBM3E.</cite> <cite index="7-11,7-12">Samsung has faced significant challenges meeting NVIDIA's qualification standards for 12-layer HBM3E due to yield and performance issues, preventing it from becoming a primary supplier.</cite> Relative call: long SK Hynix vs. short Samsung. SK's HBM franchise remains structurally superior with earlier HBM4 qualification, tighter hyperscaler relationships, and margin tailwind. Samsung's record profit disappointed because market expected closure of HBM gap; instead yield struggles persist. <cite index="38-11,38-12,38-13">SK announced 100 trillion won ($64.37B) Korea investment with M17 NAND fab starting construction 2027 and P&T7 packaging expansion to meet soaring HBM server and DRAM demand.</cite> Pair worked brutally post-Samsung earnings; SK down 14.6% vs Samsung down 9% intraday shows both caught in broad memory selloff, but SK's premium HBM positioning argues for near-term outperformance once dip-buying resumes.

memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="17-2,17-3">Q3 DRAM contract price increases decelerating to 13-18% QoQ from Q2's ~60%, driven by consumer electronics manufacturers' unwillingness to absorb higher costs rather than improved supply.</cite> <cite index="15-4">Conventional DRAM contract prices rose 93-98% QoQ in Q1 2026.</cite> <cite index="13-21">DRAM prices surged 90-95% QoQ in Q1 2026.</cite> <cite index="14-1,14-16">NAND Flash contract prices expected to rise 70-75% QoQ in Q2 2026.</cite> <cite index="15-11,15-12">First genuine sign of strain is behavioral: buyers no longer chasing higher spot quotes, NAND spot trading gone quiet, even as headline numbers stay green.</cite> <cite index="2-1,2-22">As resources are diverted to HBM, supply-demand balance for general DRAM is improving, but tightening.</cite> HBM demand growing 70% YoY continues to cannibalize conventional DRAM/NAND capacity. Cycle peak likely Q2-Q3 2026; deceleration not reversal. New capacity (Micron Idaho 2027, SK M15X pilot May 2026) arrives too late to prevent H2 plateau.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="1-2,1-6">HBM3 ~$200/stack, HBM3E ~$300/stack, HBM4 ~$500/stack as of July 2026.</cite> <cite index="3-12,3-13">Supply remains constrained through 2026, with lead times for HBM3E stacks at 20-26 weeks.</cite> <cite index="2-8,2-10">HBM3E expected to remain flagship product in 2026, accounting for approximately two-thirds of total HBM shipments, while HBM4 gradually increases share.</cite> <cite index="10-1,10-4,10-5">Samsung and SK Hynix raised 2026 HBM3E supply prices by nearly 20% in late 2025, and 2026 HBM production capacity was fully pre-booked by end-2025.</cite> <cite index="9-2,9-7">SK Hynix completed HBM4 development in September 2025, achieving performance above JEDEC's 8 Gbps baseline, giving it early qualification position.</cite> <cite index="8-5,8-15">HBM4 volume production expected late 2026 or early 2027, pushing to 16 dies per package from HBM3E's 12, a 33% increase in die consumption per chip.</cite> <cite index="4-4">Concentration of supply in three producers creates persistent undersupply expected to ease only late 2026 as all three complete capacity expansions.</cite> Pricing stable, allocation tight, HBM4 transition creates incremental wafer demand surge H2 26 into 27.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix enter bear market despite record Samsung profit guidance
news_pulse.implication: Market repricing AI infrastructure ROI timeline; memory names down >20% from recent highs despite Samsung's $59B operating profit estimate signals valuation reset underway even as fundamentals (tight supply, pricing power) remain intact through Q3.

news_pulse.headline: KOSPI circuit breaker triggered as Samsung falls 9%, SK Hynix down 14.6% intraday Tuesday
news_pulse.implication: Broad Korea tech liquidation; single-stock leveraged ETFs amplifying volatility. Dip-buyers emerged to lift SK Hynix +5.8% from lows Wednesday, Samsung +1.4%, suggesting capitulation phase may be short-lived if supply discipline holds.

news_pulse.headline: Conventional DRAM prices to rise 13-18% QoQ Q3, NAND +10-15%, major deceleration from Q2's 60% jumps
news_pulse.implication: Demand destruction emerging: consumer electronics makers unwilling to absorb further cost increases. AI server DRAM/NAND still tight, but PC/smartphone memory facing pushback. Pricing power intact but growth rate inflecting downward.

news_pulse.headline: DDR4 spot $34.80, buyers hesitant to chase higher; NAND spot trading quiet despite green prints
news_pulse.implication: Spot market signaling fatigue before contract prices roll over. Behavioral shift (buyers balking) precedes price declines by 1-2 quarters historically. Watch spot momentum for confirmation of cycle peak.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler capex $700-900B in 2026, up 36-81% YoY; Goldman raises 2025-2030 aggregate to $5.3T
news_pulse.implication: AI infrastructure arms race accelerating despite ROI questions. Amazon $200B capex guidance alone supports HBM/server DRAM demand through 2027. Sequoia's $600B revenue gap vs. AI spend widening, raising monetization risk medium-term but near-term demand visibility intact.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS capacity 120-130K wpm by end-2026, up 10x from end-2023's 13K; NVIDIA holds >60% allocation
news_pulse.implication: Advanced packaging bottleneck easing but remains binding constraint through H1 2027. NVIDIA's 60%+ CoWoS lock supports SK Hynix/Samsung HBM shipment visibility. CoWoS-L ramp for HBM4 integration critical for 2H26 B200/Rubin volume.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix announces 100 trillion won ($64.4B) Korea investment: M17 NAND fab, P&T7 packaging expansion
news_pulse.implication: SK doubling down on HBM/NAND capacity despite selloff. M17 construction starts 2027, operations targeted H1 2029. P&T7 packaging (20T won) accelerates HBM backend integration. Reinforces SK's HBM leadership strategy; contrast with Samsung's more balanced HBM/conventional mix.

news_pulse.headline: HBM 2026 capacity fully pre-booked; Samsung/SK raised HBM3E prices 20% in late 2025
news_pulse.implication: HBM pricing inflecting up even as conventional DRAM decelerates. 20% HBM3E price hike locked in for 2026 hyperscaler LTAs; insulates SK/Samsung HBM revenue from broader memory volatility. HBM ASP expansion (HBM4 $500/stack vs HBM3E $300) supports margin trajectory into 2027.

brief.derivatives_signal: Elevated put/call activity expected post-KOSPI circuit breaker. Single-stock leveraged ETFs (Samsung 2x, SK Hynix 2x) trading below 20,000 won listing price amplifies downside gamma. Wednesday's rebound (SK +5.8%, Samsung +1.4% from lows) suggests short-term capitulation, but directional bias remains fragile until US semis (MU, NVDA) stabilize. Watch KOSPI 7,600 support (broke Tuesday, closed 7,656); failure opens 7,200. Options market pricing elevated vol through SK Hynix US listing (expected Friday per market chatter), which could serve as sentiment inflection. Skew likely favoring downside protection near-term.
watch_for_next_3h: US semiconductor futures (SOX, SMH) reaction to Samsung earnings miss-on-sentiment; if US semis stabilize, Seoul dip-buyers re-emerge
TrendForce or DRAMeXchange spot pricing updates for DDR4/DDR5; any sequential decline confirms demand destruction accelerating
Hyperscaler (MSFT, AMZN, GOOGL) commentary on memory cost inflation and capex pacing—any pushback on spend validates ROI concerns
SK Hynix US listing (SKHY) timing confirmation and pricing; liquidity event could catalyze Korea-US arb flows
TSMC July 11 earnings: CoWoS utilization, HBM4 packaging readiness, and Blackwell/Rubin volume guidance will frame H2 AI chip supply
